back: Recording assets at the price originally paid, not at current value.
Old assets may be undervalued, so capital employed is too low and ROCE looks too high; comparisons may mislead.

front: Accounting policies and estimates as a limitation
back: Depreciation method and life, allowances and inventory valuation change profit and assets from the same transactions.

front: Non-financial factors not in the statements
back: Workforce skills, location, economic climate, competition, reputation, supplier relationships.
Only items that can be measured reliably in money are recorded, so non-financial factors are left out.

front: Why use historic cost at all?
back: It is objective and can be checked against source documents.
They record past transactions, but users want to predict future performance.

front: Effect of a longer estimated useful life
back: Lower depreciation each year, so higher profit and higher net book value.
